summary: Phase 9 (Stage C's first phase, NCK' rules) landed: Cslib/Logics/Modal/Metalogic/Constructive/Nested/Rules.lean defines NestedProof : NestedFull Atom -> Type u, an inductive proof-tree family indexed by conclusion, covering all 13 rules of Figure 2 (botL/id/andL/andR/orL/orRLeft/orRRight/impL/impR/boxL/boxR/diaL/diaR/contract). Each rule uses InputCtx or OutputCtx per a type-necessity argument documented in the module docstring (LHS-typed hole content needs InputCtx.fillLhs to close to a full sequent; RHS-typed content uses OutputCtx.fillRhs/fillFull directly). NestedProof.height is landed via a universally-quantified-index recursion (fixing the index via `variable` first breaks the recursive calls, since every premise has a different NestedFull index than its conclusion -- hit and fixed this session). Three smoke-test derivations landed (bare boL/id axiom instances plus one orL-on-two-botL multi-rule derivation), documented as illustrative since the source's own Section 3 text gives no literal derivation trees between Figure 2 and Proposition 3.1 to transcribe (grepped the whole PDF for 'Example' to confirm). Stage C now 1/2 complete.
decisions_made: InputCtx.fillLhs is the correct (and only well-typed) home for the 8 rules whose displayed hole-content is LHS-typed (id, botL, andL, orL, impL's 2nd premise+conclusion, boxL, diaL, contract); OutputCtx.fillRhs/fillFull for the 5 whose hole-content is RHS-typed or a full pair (andR, orRLeft/orRRight, impR, boxR) -- this is forced by argument-type necessity, not a stylistic choice, and it is what makes the botL/orL 'same subtree' side condition (noted in the source right after Figure 2) automatically satisfied with no extra Lean hypothesis.

diaR's conclusion (Gamma{diamond A-degree, [Delta]}) genuinely needs OutputCtx.fillFull, not fillRhs: NestedRhs has no comma constructor, so an RHS leaf and an LHS bracket cannot be packaged as a single fillRhs filler -- confirmed by checking NestedRhs's two constructors (atom, box) in Syntax.lean before committing to this encoding.

The plan's 'k' task-list item is read as the propositional rule family already covered by the same bullet (Figure 2 has no rule literally labelled k; that name is reserved for the Hilbert K-axiom in Constructive/CS5.lean), not a distinct rule -- documented as a plan deviation inline.

The plan's smoke-test-derivations item is scoped down to illustrative axiom/rule-combination instances rather than Proposition 3.1's full induction, because Proposition 3.1's base case needs the atomic id axiom reachable from a flat, box-free Gamma{A-input,A-output} at ctx=[], which InputCtx.fillLhs structurally cannot produce (confirmed by direct computation) -- this is a genuine standalone induction-over-formula-structure theorem, not same-phase smoke-test material.
dead_ends: Bare OutputCtx.fillLhs for any rule whose companion Pi must survive to close a full sequent: fillLhs alone only yields a NestedLhs, not a NestedFull -- type error, not a design choice.

Building diaR's conclusion via OutputCtx.fillRhs applied to some crafted NestedRhs term mixing Delta and the diamond-atom: impossible, NestedRhs has only atom/box constructors, no comma -- confirmed by direct inspection of Syntax.lean before attempting this route.

Proving Gamma{A-input,A-output} derivable via impR+id at ctx=[] as a 'quick' smoke test for a general formula A: fails structurally, since InputCtx.fillLhs always forces one mandatory box between the hole and ctx.pi, so id's conclusion is never flat/box-free -- this is Proposition 3.1's actual base-case obstruction, not a shortcut worth re-attempting without the full induction machinery.
